role: Environmental Analysis Section, Programs Development Division, Bureau of Wastewater & Stream Quality Control, SC DHEC
stance_basis: letter raises three specific environmental concerns requiring additional evidence or analysis before the project can be adequately assessed
summary: C. Barry Shedrow of SC DHEC's Environmental Analysis Section submitted a letter dated April 20, 1976 raising three specific environmental concerns about the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project: the need for evidence supporting shoreline stabilization claims, the need to address mercury level impacts from increased sedimentation, and the need to consider sediment accumulation effects on lake stratification. The agency did not oppose the project outright but requested additional analysis and supporting evidence on these points.
complaint_summary: Shedrow raises three concerns: (1) lack of evidence supporting the one-year shoreline stabilization claim for Bad Creek Reservoir, (2) failure to address mercury level impacts on receiving waters and biota from increased sedimentation in Howard Creek and Lake Jocassee, and (3) failure to consider how sediment accumulation at the submerged weir could alter discharge patterns and affect lake stratification.

statement.text:
This office has reviewed the Draft Environmental Impact Statement regarding the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Hydroelectric Project and offers the following comments for your consideration:
(1) on Page 3-28, it is indicated that shoreline stabilization in the Bed Creek Reservoir will probably be realized within one year of initiation of plant operations. Evidence supporting this expectation should be presented.
(2) construction of the Bad Creek Project will result in increased sedimentation within Howard Creek and downstream Lake Jocassee. The effects of this sediment influx upon the mercury levels of both receiving waters and indigenous biota should be addressed.
(3) sediment accumulation at the submerged weir may eventually alter discharge patterns into Lake Jocassee. The possible impact of this phenomenon upon lake stratification should be considered.
We appreciate the opportunity to have commented on thus matter.
C. Day Shehow
C. Barry Shedrow
Environmental Analysis Section 
Programs Development Division
Bureau of Wastewater & Stream Quality
Control
